text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL) has accused the finance ministry of manipulating last year's budget deficit figures, saying the shortfall was much higher than recently published preliminary figures showing a 26.98 billion crown deficit.

- The SDL said it would present an amendment to the law on privatisation of strategic companies which should ensure the four state-controlled Slovak financial institutions will not be privatised after March 31, when the current law barring the sell-offs expires.

- Minor opposition party Social Democrats (SDSS) accused the majority owner of oil and gas storage company Nafta of trying to sell the firm to an unspecified German company. Nafta officials and representatives of Ruhrgas, which was originally interested in the firm's privatisation, rejected the charge.

- Cellulose maker SCP Ruzomberok a.s. said it expected a gross profit of some 500 million crowns for 1996, down from 2.2 billion in 1995. The company said the profit decline was due to lower world cellulose prices.

PRAVDA - Central bank Vice-governor Marian Jusko said the current development with the interbank interest rates was an expected reaction to the bank's monetary programme for 1997. He said such a reaction shortly after announcing the programme last December was expected and not with a one month delay, adding that that is why the upward jump was so significant.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Some interbank dealers expect rates on the interbank money market to rise even further by the end of January, from the current level of about 26 percent, as banks which did not fulfill their minimum reserves requirements in mid January start seeking crowns on the illiquid market.
- The Slovak-Ukraine trade volume totalled $23.5 million last year, some $4.2 million less than in 1995.
